newsitem.title: USA: Uncle B's says sees Q4, FY96 loss.
newsitem.headline: Uncle B's says sees Q4, FY96 loss.

text.p: Uncle B's Bakery Inc said Thursday it will have a loss for the fourth quarter and fiscal year 1996 ended July 31.

The loss primarily stems from greater-than-planned expenses with plant expansion, new packaging processes and the startup of production and development of the new frozen, bake-off line of bagels, chief executive officer William Rose Jr said in a news rlease.

The company said it had sales of $17.4 million in fiscal 1996 versus $15.3 million in 1995. The company reported a profit of $0.11 a share for fiscal 1995 and $0.05 a share in the fourth quarter, after a $0.15 a share gain on refinancing of long-term debt.

"Due to costs in product development, the startup of our new line and packaging issues associated with the Resealable Zip Strip, Uncle B's will experience lower-than-expected sales and a significant loss in the fourth quarter and for the year," Rose said in a news release. "Although we finished this year with disappointing results, we are confident that we are now better positioned for future growth."
